title: Review the RSVP function
prompt: This version of `lantern-rsvp` was opened as a pull request. It looks almost identical to the lesson's function, but three lines would cause a security incident, a growing bill, or broken RSVPs in production. Select them.
hints: How should a Lambda function get its credentials?
Which DynamoDB operation reads the whole table, and which reads one partition?
Read the condition expression aloud: the write succeeds only if the item ... ?
explanation: Line 5 hard-codes an access key into the client. The function already has an execution role, and the SDK uses it automatically when you pass no credentials, so delete the `credentials` option entirely; never put keys in code or environment variables. Line 19 counts RSVPs with a `Scan` and a filter, which reads and bills every item in the table on every page view; use `QueryCommand` with `KeyConditionExpression: "eventId = :e"` and `Select: "COUNT"`. (A Scan also stops after 1 MB, so on a big table this count would be wrong as well as expensive.) Line 36 inverts the duplicate guard: `attribute_exists(email)` lets a write succeed only when the RSVP already exists, so every new RSVP fails with 409. It must be `attribute_not_exists(email)`.
